label: copy phase: letter c fed back as the 2nd/3rd copied token
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase when the input token is the letter c, i.e. when c is being fed back as original token 1 or 2 (recall_idx 2-3), and a further output remains (not the final step). Strongest when c is original token 1 (input two steps after <DEL>; ~60% of mass, top examples all of form x c ... <DEL> x [c]); weaker at original token 2, weak/near-threshold when c is original token 3 (recall_idx 4) or token 0 (recall_idx 1), essentially silent at later positions. Never fires in the original phase or on the delimiter, never on any input token other than c, and not on the last copy step. Independent of the output token, L, and digit count.

issues: The claims hold up. All activation is in the copy phase and only when the input is c (rate 0.177, lift 32.7x). No other input token, the original phase or the delimiter ever activates it.

Mass by recall_idx matches the explanation: recall_idx 2 has 60.4% (precision 0.975 when c is the input), recall_idx 3 has 37.1% (precision 0.85), recall_idx 4 has 2.3% (precision 0.33) and recall_idx 1 has 0.15% (precision 0.03). recall_idx 5 and above are essentially silent.
The claim that it never fires on the last copy step is confirmed: c with recall_idx 3 and to_go 0 has precision 0.0004.

Minor imprecision: the predicate misses 15% of active steps by count, mostly weak recall_idx 4 activations (the bottom quartile of activations is only 42% covered). These hold 2.5% of the mass and fire inconsistently (precision 0.33, graded by L, near zero at L=5). Adding recall_idx 4 lowers test F1 to 0.905, so leaving it out is reasonable.
The 15 test false positives are short-L cases at the edge of the window. This is scattered noise, not a systematic class.
